answer: The oasis test I would run is Proof of unique Stack Exchange moderation history: flags and reviews handled across years, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so flags and reviews handled across years stays private; the canyon is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the lantern of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
